questions.stem: Which of the following compounds will undergo nucleophilic substitution ( $\mathrm{S_N1}$ ) fastest?
questions.solution: The rate of $\mathrm{S_N1}$ depends on the stability of the carbocation intermediate. Benzyl carbocation ($\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2^+}$) is highly stabilized by resonance over the benzene ring, which is more effective than the allylic system and secondary alkyl systems, making benzyl chloride undergo $\mathrm{S_N1}$ faster than the others listed. Chlorobenzene does not undergo nucleophilic substitution under standard conditions.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds will undergo nucleophilic substitution ($S_N2$) reaction fastest?
questions.solution: $S_N2$ substitution kinetics are highly sensitive to steric hindrance. Primary alkyl halides without branching on the adjacent carbon atom react the fastest. Thus, 1-chlorobutane ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_2Cl}$) is less hindered than isobutyl chloride ($\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CHCH_2Cl}$), secondary, or tertiary chlorides, and undergoes the fastest $S_N2$ reaction.

questions.stem: Among the following, the one which is most reactive towards nucleophilic substitution ($\mathrm{S_N2}$) reaction is:
questions.solution:
The reactivity of alkyl halides towards $\mathrm{S_N2}$ mechanism decreases with increasing steric hindrance: Primary ($1^\circ$) > Secondary ($2^\circ$) > Tertiary ($3^\circ$).
$\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{Cl}$ is a straight-chain $1^\circ$ alkyl halide, hence it is the most reactive towards $\mathrm{S_N2}$ substitution.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds will undergo nucleophilic substitution ($S_{\mathrm{N}}1$) fastest?
questions.solution: $S_{\mathrm{N}}1$ reactions proceed via a carbocation intermediate. The order of stability of carbocations formed is: Benzyl carbocation ($\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2^+}$) is highly stabilized by resonance over the benzene ring, more so than the allyl carbocation ($\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH_2^+}$) which has only one double bond for resonance. Hence, benzyl chloride reacts fastest.

questions.stem: The correct order of reactivity towards $\mathrm{S_N2}$ displacement reaction is:
questions.solution: $\mathrm{S_N2}$ reactivity is highly sensitive to steric hindrance around the carbon bearing the leaving group. The order of reactivity is $1^\circ > 2^\circ > 3^\circ$ alkyl halides. Hence, 1-bromobutane ($1^\circ$) > 2-bromobutane ($2^\circ$) > 2-bromo-2-methylpropane ($3^\circ$).

questions.stem:
For the reaction: $R-\text{X} + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow R-\text{OH} + \text{X}^-$, the rate of reaction of alkyl halides in $S_N2$ reaction decreases in the order:
$\text{CH}_3\text{X} > \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{X} > (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHX} > (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CX}$
If the rate of reaction of $R-\text{X}$ with $\text{OH}^-$ in $S_N2$ mechanism is represented as $\text{Rate} = k[R-\text{X}][\text{OH}^-]$, then the relative rate of reaction of $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-CH}_2\text{Cl}$ with $\text{OH}^-$ compared to $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$ under identical $S_N2$ conditions is found to be exceptionally low (nearly $10^{-5}$ times). The factor of 10 with a power $-x$ represents this ratio. The value of $x$ is _______. (Nearest Integer)
questions.solution:
Neopentyl chloride, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCH}_2\text{Cl}$, is a primary alkyl halide but has extremely high steric hindrance due to the bulky tert-butyl group adjacent to the reaction center.
Its relative rate compared to ethyl chloride is approximately $10^{-5}$ times.
Comparing with $10^{-x}$, we get $x = 5$.

questions.stem:
The correct order of reactivity of the following alkyl halides towards $\mathrm{S_N2}$ reaction is:
(I) $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{Br}$
(II) $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\mathrm{CHCH}_2\mathrm{Br}$
(III) $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}_3)\mathrm{Br}$
(IV) $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_3\mathrm{CBr}$
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{S_N2}$ reactivity depends heavily on steric hindrance around the leaving group carbon:
- (I) $1^\circ$ unbranched: least hindered, fastest.
- (II) $1^\circ$ with branch at $\beta$-carbon: more hindered than (I).
- (III) $2^\circ$ halide: highly hindered.
- (IV) $3^\circ$ halide: extremely hindered, negligible rate.
Thus, reactivity order: I > II > III > IV.

questions.stem: The rate of $S_N1$ reaction is fastest for which of the following halides?
questions.solution: The rate of $S_N1$ reaction depends on the stability of the carbocation formed in the rate-determining step. Allyl chloride forms the allyl carbocation ($\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH_2^+}$), which is resonance stabilized and much more stable than the isopropyl carbocation (secondary) or n-propyl carbocation (primary). Chlorobenzene does not undergo $S_N1$ readily.

questions.stem: The correct order of reactivity of the following alkyl halides towards $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$ reaction is :
questions.solution:
$\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$ reaction rate is governed by steric hindrance at the reaction center. The less steric hindrance, the faster the reaction. The order is:
$\text{Methyl halide} > 1^{\circ} \text{ halide} > 2^{\circ} \text{ halide} > 3^{\circ} \text{ halide}$.
Hence: $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl} > \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} > (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCl} > (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCl}$.

questions.stem: Which of the following alkyl halides undergoes $\mathrm{S_N1}$ reaction most rapidly?
questions.solution: For a given alkyl group, the rate of nucleophilic substitution (both $\mathrm{S_N1}$ and $\mathrm{S_N2}$) depends on the leaving group ability: $\mathrm{I^- > Br^- > Cl^- > F^-}$. Thus, tert-butyl iodide reacts most rapidly.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds will undergo $S_{\text{N}}1$ reaction most readily?
questions.solution: The rate of $S_{\text{N}}1$ reaction depends on the stability of the carbocation intermediate. Since the tertiary carbocation $(CH_3)_3C^+$ is highly stable due to hyperconjugation and inductive effect, $(CH_3)_3C-Cl$ undergoes $S_{\text{N}}1$ most readily.

questions.stem: Which of the following alkyl halides undergoes nucleophilic substitution by $\mathrm{S_N1}$ mechanism fastest?
questions.solution: $\mathrm{S_N1}$ reaction rates depend on the stability of the carbocation intermediate and the leaving group ability. Tertiary carbocation $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C^+}$ is highly stable, and $\mathrm{I^-}$ is an excellent leaving group compared to $\mathrm{Cl^-}$. Hence, tert-butyl iodide undergoes $\mathrm{S_N1}$ fastest.

questions.stem: The correct order of reactivity of the following alkyl halides towards $S_N2$ reaction is:
questions.solution: $S_N2$ reactivity depends primarily on steric hindrance around the carbon bearing the leaving group. The order of steric hindrance is Primary ($1^\circ$) < Secondary ($2^\circ$) < Tertiary ($3^\circ$). Therefore, the reactivity order is: 1-bromobutane ($1^\circ$) > 2-bromobutane ($2^\circ$) > 2-bromo-2-methylpropane ($3^\circ$).

questions.stem: Which of the following alkyl halides undergoes $\mathrm{S_N1}$ reaction most rapidly?
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{S_N1}$ reactions proceed via a carbocation intermediate. The rate of the reaction depends on the stability of the carbocation formed.
$(\mathrm{CH}_3)_3\mathrm{C-Cl}$ forms a stable tertiary carbocation, $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_3\mathrm{C}^+$, and thus reacts fastest.

questions.stem: Which of the following alkyl halides undergoes nucleophilic substitution by $\mathrm{S_N1}$ mechanism at the fastest rate?
questions.solution: The rate of $\mathrm{S_N1}$ depends on the stability of the carbocation formed. Allyl chloride forms the allyl carbocation ($\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH_2^+}$), which is resonance stabilized, making it undergo $\mathrm{S_N1}$ much faster than ethyl or isopropyl chlorides.

questions.stem: Which of the following alkyl halides undergoes nucleophilic substitution reaction by $\mathrm{S_N1}$ mechanism most rapidly?
questions.solution: The rate of $\mathrm{S_N1}$ reactions is determined by the stability of the intermediate carbocation. The order of carbocation stability is $3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ > \text{methyl}$. tert-Butyl chloride forms a highly stable tertiary carbocation, so it reacts most rapidly via $\mathrm{S_N1}$.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds undergoes nucleophilic substitution ($S_N1$) fastest?
questions.solution: $S_N1$ reactions proceed via a carbocation intermediate. The order of stability of carbocations is $3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ > \text{methyl}$. Therefore, tert-butyl chloride forms the highly stable tert-butyl carbocation and undergoes $S_N1$ fastest.
